title: Find K Closest Elements
prompt: Given a sorted integer array `arr`, two integers `k` and `x`, return the `k` closest integers to `x` in the array, sorted in ascending order. An integer `a` is closer to `x` than an integer `b` if `abs(a - x) < abs(b - x)`, or `abs(a - x) == abs(b - x)` and `a < b`.

examples.explanation: When k equals the length of arr, every element must be included, regardless of x.

constraints: arr is sorted in ascending order
hints: Sorting all elements by distance to x and taking the first k works, but costs O(n log n) when the array is already sorted and a window-based approach could do better.
The answer is always a contiguous window of k elements in the sorted array, so instead of searching for individual elements, binary search for the starting index of that window.

For a candidate window start `lo`, compare x - arr[lo] to arr[lo + k] - x: if the left element is farther from x than the right candidate, the window should shift right; otherwise the current window (or one further left) is at least as good.

solution.approach: Because arr is sorted, the k closest elements always form one contiguous subarray of length k. Binary search over the possible starting index of that window, in the range [0, len(arr) - k]. For a candidate start `lo`, compare the distance of the window's left edge (x - arr[lo]) to the distance of the element just past the window's right edge (arr[lo + k] - x): if the left edge is farther, shifting the window right strictly improves it, so move lo up; otherwise keep or shrink toward lo. This converges to the optimal window start in O(log(n - k)) time.
